newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans prefer neither Kohl nor Lafontaine-poll.
newsitem.headline: Germans prefer neither Kohl nor Lafontaine-poll.

text.p: Germans see neither Chancellor Helmut Kohl nor opposition leader Oskar Lafontaine as the best candidates in next year's general election and prefer their number two men instead, a poll said on Thursday.

The Forsa poll in the weekly Die Woche said only 28 percent of those surveyed saw Kohl as the best candidate for his Christian Democrats (CDU) while 31 percent wanted his crown prince, CDU parliamentary leader Wolfgang Schaeuble, to run.
For the opposition Social Democrats (SPD), 48 percent said they wanted Lower Saxony state premier Gerhard Schroeder to run compared to only 27 percent for party chairman Lafontaine.
Broken down by party membership, the poll showed strong support for Kohl within his own party, with 63 percent of CDU members preferring him and only 24 percent backing Schaeuble.
Only 36 percent of SPD voters preferred Lafontaine compared to 52 percent who backed Schroeder.
Kohl, who has been chancellor since 1982, has not yet said whether he will run again but seemed to hint he would in speech he gave to CDU deputies on Tuesday.
The Forsa poll was conducted on February 14-17 with a sample of 1,014 people and margin of three percent.
